The University of Iowa's 2026-27 resident undergraduate tuition and fees are about $11,971, but the university's own cost pages still show an older figure.

- **Regents figure:** The Board of Regents' 2026-27 table puts Iowa resident base tuition at $9,852 plus $2,119 in mandatory fees, for $11,971 total ([Regents agenda item](https://www.iowaregents.edu/media/cms/0426_ITEM_8__Tuition_Fees_33E237082BA3C.pdf)). That is a $349 increase over 2025-26.

That matches the 2025-26 Regents figure, so the university pages may not yet reflect the new rate.
- **Program variations:** Some programs carry different rates. The Tippie College of Business is setting a base resident rate of $13,052 for BBA students, and new economics majors face $11,852 ([University of Iowa News](https://now.uiowa.edu/node/58381)).

The Rutgers Board of Governors approved a 3% tuition increase for in-state and out-of-state students for 2026-27, its lowest increase in four years. The budget took effect July 1, 2026.

For a typical full-time New Brunswick School of Arts and Sciences New Jersey resident, tuition is projected to rise on average $448 for the academic year, from $14,933 to $15,381. Average mandatory fees are estimated to increase by about $117 annually, from $3,891 to $4,008. Adding those two figures gives roughly $19,389 in tuition plus mandatory fees (my calculation, not a published number). Fees vary by program, so other schools will differ.

Other details from the same coverage:
- Housing and dining expenses are projected to rise 4%, from $15,332 to $15,945.
- Students with family adjusted gross income up to $65,000 pay zero for tuition and mandatory fees through income gap-bridging programs, including the Scarlet Guarantee in New Brunswick.
- The official Rutgers admissions page still shows 2025-26 figures, with tuition of $14,933 and fees of $3,891 for New Jersey residents. Per-school 2025-26 rate schedules are also posted, but I did not find a published 2026-27 school-by-school schedule.

- **$12,664 (UW Finance):** The official finance page lists resident annual tuition at $12,664 for [the Seattle campus, the 2026-27 budget table](https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/node/24790). Its Seattle resident annual total is $37,680. That page says the figures were approved by the Board of Regents in June 2026 and that the state's allowed resident undergraduate tuition increase for the year is 3.3%.
- **$13,406 (UW Admissions):** The admissions budget page gives [resident tuition of $13,406 for the nine-month year](https://admit.washington.edu/?p=76), with a resident total of $36,746 for students living on or off campus. A [UW cost-of-attendance page](https://www.washington.edu/financialaid/cost-of-attendance/) lists tuition and fees at $13,873, which is a different combined figure.

Nonresident tuition is also listed two ways. The finance page gives [$44,580](https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/files/docs/cost-of-attendance-for-the-2026-27-academic-year.docx), while admissions and a third-party source give [$44,460](https://admit.washington.edu/costs/coa).

The likely explanation is that the figures measure different things, such as tuition alone versus tuition plus certain fees or a nine-month versus annual basis. I could not confirm which is correct from these results. For an authoritative answer, check UW's Current Tuition and Fees Dashboard or Student Financial Aid. Note that one source here, collegedunia, is a third-party site, and uni2study is a blog.
